title: The Bionic Clicker Mark I & II
protocol: Plug the bio-signals sensor shield into the microcontroller.
Screw the EMG cables into the E, M and GND screw terminals of the shield.
Place a row of three header pins into the muscle sensor in the +, - and SIG holes from above.
Solder underneath the header pins placed into the muscle sensor.
Bend the header pins 90 ° with a pair of plyers halfway up the pins.
Cut the three EMG cables with a wire cutter to run from the wrist to the back of the hand.
Strip the end of the three EMG cables with a wire stripper.
Place the stripped black wire into the R hole of the muscle sensor.
Place the stripped blue wire into the E hole of the muscle sensor.
Place the stripped red wire into the M hole of the muscle sensor.
Solder the wires in place on the underside of the muscle sensor.
Clip two electrode pads into the underside of the muscle sensor.
Attach one electrode to the connector of the black reference cable.
Stick the muscle sensor onto the selected muscle with the electrode pads.
Place the black reference electrode in an appropriate location.
Cut 8 single-core multi-thread wires to length and strip each end: 5 short (7 cm) wires for microcontroller to control board, 3 longer (approximately 12 cm) wires for wrist connections.
Place two red wires into the 3V hole of the microcontroller.
Place two black wires into the GND hole of the microcontroller.
Place the long green wire into the A0 hole of the microcontroller.
Place the short blue wire into the 2 hole of the microcontroller.
Place the long white wire into the 3 hole of the microcontroller.
Place the short green wire into the 5 hole of the microcontroller.
Solder the wires in place on the underside of the microcontroller.
Solder the red wire to the first header socket.
Solder the black wire to the second header socket.
Solder the green wire to the third header socket.
Place EMG sensor pads on the hand with two electrodes at either end of the abductor indicis muscle.
Attach one EMG sensor pad in the middle of the back of the hand.
Clip the blue and red electrodes above the muscle.
Clip the black electrode on the back of the hand.
Download the library for the bio-signals shield from the reference section link14.
Unzip the downloaded library and place it in the Arduino libraries folder.
Add microcontroller boards to the Integrated Development (IDE) following instructions15.
Download 'ThresholdTest.ino' for MK I or 'BLEThresholdTest.ino' and 'BluefruitConfig.h' for MK II.
Open the downloaded files in the IDE software.
Unplug the laptop from the mains power supply.
Plug the microcontroller into the laptop via a USB cable.
Upload the relevant version of the threshold test to the microcontroller.
Open the serial monitor (Tools>Serial Monitor) to display EMG output.
Move the index finger from side to side.
Move the hand around without moving the index finger.
Write down the values displayed in each case.
Check that cables are not moving to avoid noise interference.
Select a value above what is seen when the hand moves but below what is seen when the finger moves.
Write down this selected value as the Threshold Trigger Value.
Adjust the gain setting if necessary to find an appropriate threshold value.
Replace electrodes if needed and set abductor indicis muscle gain to minimum initially.
Alter the gain setting using a small flat-head screwdriver on the GAIN potentiometer.
Download 'BoomTest.ino' for MK I or 'BLEBoomTest.ino' and BluefruitConfig.h for MK II.
Edit the provided code by replacing 'PLACE_YOUR_THRESHOLD_TRIGGER_VALUE_HERE' with the determined Threshold Trigger Value.
Upload the correct version of BoomTest to the microcontroller.
Open the serial monitor in the IDE software (Tools>Serial Monitor).
Move the hand around without moving the index finger from side to side.
Move the index finger from side to side.
Download stl files for all 5 components of the MK II case.
Print the parts of the MK II case by any preferred method.
Place a row of two header pins on the underside of the control board.
Solder five 10 KΩ resistors to the control board.
Solder a sliding switch onto the control board.
Solder two push button switches to the control board.
Slice through copper tracks on the strip board following grey lines on Figure 8A with a craft knife.
Cut 7 wires of correct length for running from forearm to upper arm (around 30 cm).
Cut a red wire of 7 cm length.
Cut a black wire of 3 cm length.
Cut an orange and a blue wire each of 4 cm length.
Strip both ends of the cut wires with a wire stripper.
Place the wires in the control board according to the circuit diagram.
Solder the wires in place on the underside of the board.
Solder the long red and black wires to a pair of header pins.
Solder the other long wires to a strip of header pins in the order: blue, orange, white, brown, yellow.
Solder the 5V and GND pins of the wireless module to the header pins on the control board.
Solder the short orange wire to pin 2 of the wireless communication module.
Solder the short blue wire to pin 3 of the wireless communication module.
Place three 10 KΩ resistors, a sliding switch, and two push button switches according to Figure 10A.
Solder them into place on the underside of the board.
Break the copper tracks on the strip board by slicing through with a craft knife, following the grey lines on Figure 10A.

Cut the wires previously soldered to the microcontroller with a wire cutter so that they can run through the mid layer of the microcontroller case to the control board without stopping the case from closing (Figure 10B).
Place the wires in the control board according to the circuit diagram.
Solder the wires in place.
Re-assemble the Bionic Clicker.
Connect the header connectors from the control board wires to the microcontroller and bio-signals shield.
Connect the battery to the microcontroller.
Move on to step 6.3.
Connect the header connector from the microcontroller to the muscle sensor (green wire to SIG).
Connect the microcontroller to the laptop via USB cable.
Download 'BionicClicker.ino' or 'BLEBionicClicker.ino and BluefruitConfig.h'.
Open the downloaded code in the IDE software.
Edit the code and replace 'PLACE_YOUR_THRESHOLD_TRIGGER_VALUE_HERE' with the Threshold Trigger Value determined in step 2.7 (on line 59 of the code for the MK I, line 83 of the code for the MK II).
Disconnect the microcontroller from the laptop by removing the USB cable.
If using the MK I, follow the instructions to pair the wireless module to the device by following the manufacturer's guide.
If using the MK II, connect to the device wirelessly following the procedure to connect a wireless keyboard to the computer being used.
Attach the control board to the wrist strap.
Attach the microcontroller and battery to the upper arm strap.
Plug the 9 V battery into the microcontroller with the PP3 connector.
Connect the microcontroller and e-health shield to the control board via soldered wires.
Cut double-sided hook and loop material 35 mm wide and long enough to wrap around the wrist (around 22 cm for smaller wrists).
Slide the hook and loop material through the clips at the bottom of the case, with loops facing inwards.
Plug the wires soldered to the microcontroller into the male header pins on the muscle sensor.
Clip the electrodes into the EMG cables by pushing them on.
